{{Short description|Annual cricket tournament}} {{Use dmy dates|date=July 2016}} {{Infobox cricket tournament main | name = Dhaka Premier Division Cricket League | image = Dhaka Premier Division Cricket League 2019-20.jpg | country = [[Bangladesh]] | administrator = [[Bangladesh Cricket Board]] | cricket format = [[List A cricket|List A]] | first = 1973–74
2013–14 (as List A competition) | last = [[2021–22 Dhaka Premier Division Cricket League|2021–22]] | next = [[2022–23 Dhaka Premier Division Cricket League|2022–23]] | tournament format = Round Robin | participants = 12 | champions = [[Sheikh Jamal Dhanmondi Club cricket team|Sheikh Jamal Dhanmondi Club]] (1st title) | most successful = [[Abahani Limited cricket team|Abahani Limited]] (3 titles) | most runs = | most wickets = | TV =Tsports & GTV | website = | current = |Sponsor=Walton}} The '''Dhaka Premier Division Cricket League''', also known as the '''Dhaka Premier League''', is a club [[List A cricket|List A]] tournament in [[Bangladesh]].{{cite web| url = http://www.tigercricket.com/domestic/dhaka-premier-league| title = Walton Dhaka Premier Division Cricket League 2014| publisher = Bangladesh Cricket Board| access-date = 2 March 2015| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150225030809/http://www.tigercricket.com/domestic/bangladesh-cricket-league/| archive-date = 25 February 2015| url-status = dead}} ==History== Since its inauguration in 1973–74 the league has been the premier club cricket competition in [[Bangladesh]].{{cite web |last1=Isam |first1=Mohammad |title=The original premier league |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/mohammad-isam-on-the-dhaka-premier-league-1101714 |website=Cricinfo |access-date=6 March 2022}} It gained [[List A cricket|List A]] status starting with the 2013–14 tournament, thus superseding the [[National Cricket League One-Day]] as Bangladesh's main List A competition. In the years from 1973–74 to 2011–12, [[Abahani Limited cricket team|Abahani Limited]] won the championship 17 times.{{cite web|last1=Isam|first1=Mohammad|title=No restriction on Pakistan players in Dhaka Premier League|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/21855742/no-restriction-pakistan-players-dhaka-premier-league|website=Cricinfo|access-date=28 March 2015}} Other winners were [[Mohammedan Sporting Club cricket team|Mohammedan Sporting Club]] nine times, [[Biman Bangladesh Airlines cricket team|Biman Bangladesh Airlines]] five times, [[Victoria Sporting Club]] four times, [[Old DOHS Sports Club]] twice and [[Brothers Union cricket team|Brothers Union]] once. There was no tournament in 2012–13. To commemorate the centenary of the birth of the founding father of Bangladesh, [[Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman]], the 2019–20 season of the league was named "Bangabandhu Dhaka Premier Division Cricket League 2019–20".{{cite web |title=General guideline |url=http://www.tigercricket.com.bd/wp-content/uploads/2020/02/GENERAL-GUIDELINE-Bangabandhu-Dhaka-Premier-Division-Cricket-League-2019-20-DPDCL-2020-21-2021-22.pdf |website=Tiger Cricket |access-date=6 March 2020}} However, the competition was postponed shortly after starting and later abandoned, owing to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. The next tournament, in 2021–22, was officially named the "Bangabandhu Dhaka Premier Division Cricket League 2021–2022 sponsored by Walton". ==List A winners== Since the tournament gained List A status, the winners have been: * 2013–14: [[Gazi Tank Cricketers]]{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/bangladesh/content/story/694409.html |title=Morgan stars in Gazi Tank's title win |work=ESPN cricinfo |date=29 November 2013}} * 2014–15: [[Prime Bank Cricket Club|Prime Bank]]{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/dhaka-premier-division-2014-15/content/story/816493.html |title=Soumya Sarkar leads Prime Bank to title win |work=ESPN cricinfo |date=4 January 2015}} * 2015–16: [[Abahani Limited cricket team|Abahani Limited]]{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/bangladesh-domestic-2016-17/content/story/1028531.html |title=Abahani thump Prime Bank to lift 18th title |work=ESPN cricinfo |date=23 June 2016}} * [[2016–17 Dhaka year, can only start in January – Khaled Mahmud |work=ESPN cricinfo |date=20 October 2020}} * [[2020–21 Dhaka Premier Division Cricket League|2020–21]]: ''cancelled due to COVID-19 pandemic'' * [[2021–22 Dhaka Premier Division Cricket League|2021–22]]: [[Sheikh Jamal Dhanmondi Club cricket team|Sheikh Jamal Dhanmondi Club]] * [[2022–23 Dhaka Premier Division Cricket League|2022–23]]: ''in progress'' Notes: This competition was played in the early part of the season in both 2013–14 and 2014–15. Starting in 2016, it is now played during the spring months each year. ==Format== The competition is played as a round-robin, followed by play-off rounds among the top six teams for the championship and among the lowest three teams to determine [[Promotion and relegation|relegation]]. The 2013–14 competition ran from September to November 2014; the 2014–15 competition ran from November 2014 to January 2015; the 2015–16 competition ran from April to June 2016; the 2016–17 competition ran from April to June 2017; the 2017–18 competition ran from February to April 2018; the 2018–19 competition ran from March to April 2019; the 2019–20 competition began in March 2020, but was almost immediately postponed owing to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]; the next tournament, 2021–22, ran from March to April 2022. All matches are played on neutral grounds in the [[Dhaka]] area. In 2016–17 only three grounds were used: [[Khan Shaheb Osman Ali Stadium]] in [[Fatullah]], and [[Bangladesh Krira Shikkha Protisthan cricket grounds#Bangladesh Krira Shikkha Protisthan No 3 Ground|Bangladesh Krira Shikkha Protisthan No 3]] and [[Bangladesh Krira Shikkha Protisthan cricket grounds#Bangladesh Krira Shikkha Protisthan No 4 Ground|No 4 Grounds]] in [[Savar Upazila|Savar]]. The same three grounds were used in 2017–18 and 2018–19, as well as [[Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium]] in [[Mirpur Model Thana|Mirpur]]. ==Players== The system of allocating players to clubs varies from season to season, but has elements of lottery.{{cite web|last1=Isam|first1=Mohammad|title='Players by choice' transfer set to return in Dhaka league|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/bangladesh/content/story/994009.html|website=Cricinfo|access-date=22 April 2016}}{{cite web|last1=Isam|first1=Mohammad|title=BCB reverts to draft system for player transfers in DPL|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/21949686/bcb-reverts-draft-system-player-transfers-dpl|website=Cricinfo|access-date=4 January 2018}}{{cite web |title=Rules for the players' draft event |url=http://www.tigercricket.com.bd/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/Rules-of-PLAYERS-DRAFT-Event-2019.docx.pdf |website=TigerCricket |publisher=Bangladesh Cricket Board |access-date=21 March 2019}} Players frequently change clubs between seasons. [[Imrul Kayes]], for example, played for [[Victoria Sporting Club cricket team|Victoria Sporting Club ]] in 2006–07 and 2014–15, [[Mohammedan Sporting Club cricket team|Mohammedan Sporting Club]] in 2007–08, 2011–12 and 2022–23, [[Gazi Tank Cricketers]] in 2008–09 and 2013–14, [[Abahani Limited cricket team|Abahani Limited]] in 2009–10 and 2010–11, [[Brothers Union cricket team|Brothers Union]] in 2015–16, [[Sheikh Jamal Dhanmondi Club cricket team|Sheikh Jamal Dhanmondi Club]] in 2016–17 and 2021–22, and [[Gazi Group Cricketers]] in 2017–18 and 2018–19.{{cite web|title=List A matches played by Imrul Kayes|url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/163/163657/List_A_Matches.html|website=Cricket Archive|access-date=28 March 2023}} Of the 22 players who appeared for [[Brothers Union cricket team|Brothers Union]] in 2013–14,{{cite web|title=Batting for Brothers Union 2013–14|url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Events/20/Dhaka_Premier_Division_2013-14/Brothers_Union_Batting.html|website=CricketArchive|access-date=9 April 2015}} only two were among the 20 Brothers Union players in 2014–15.{{cite web|title=Batting for Brothers Union 2014–15|url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Events/23/Dhaka_Premier_Division_2014-15/Brothers_Union_Batting.html|website=CricketArchive|access-date=9 April 2015}} From the 1980s to the 2019–20 competition most teams included players from outside Bangladesh. In 2013–14 82 foreign players played in the competition.''Wisden India Almanack 2015'', p. 117. Beginning with the 2015–16 competition, only one foreign player has been allowed in any playing eleven, although clubs are allowed to have several foreign players on their list;{{cite web|last1=Isam|first1=Mohammad|title=Manoj Tiwary signed by Abahani Limited to play Dhaka Premier League|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/bangladesh-domestic-2016-17/content/story/1014795.html|website=Cricinfo|access-date=21 May 2016}} in 2015–16 36 foreign players took part, including 22 Indians and 10 Sri Lankans.{{cite web|last1=Isam|first1=Mohammad|last2=Kishore|first2=Shashank|title=Indians dominate overseas presence in DPL|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/bangladesh/content/story/1029853.html|website=Cricinfo|access-date=27 June 2016}} Foreign players were excluded from the 2019–20 competition,{{cite news |date=23 February 2020|title=Premier Cricket League: No foreign cricketer allowed this year |url=https://www.unb.com.bd/category/Sports/premier-cricket-league-no-foreign-cricketer-allowed-this-year/45113 |work=UNB |access-date=6 March 2020}} but were allowed again for the 2021–22 competition, with no more than one foreign player per team.{{cite news |title=Bangabandhu DPL to kick off today |url=https://www.observerbd.com/details.php?id=357363 |access-date=15 March 2022 |work=The Daily Observer |date=15 March 2022}} ==Teams== There are 12 participating teams, changing each season with promotion and relegation. The two lowest-finishing teams are demoted to the second division (known as the Dhaka First Division League) for the next season and the top two teams in the second division are promoted.
